name: Monad
executive_summary: Monad's mainnet launched on November 24, 2025, under a year old at the time of this scoring, built specifically for high-throughput, parallelized transaction execution. That focus shows up in an Execution Layer score of 86 and an AI score of 72, fast and reliable enough to settle transactions in about 600 milliseconds. The TradFi score of 50 tells a different story: insiders hold roughly half the token supply behind a single cliff that unlocks about 1.4 times the current circulating supply in a single day on November 24, 2026, and that concentration is the single biggest drag on the score -- offset partly by a validator set that is open to anyone, though concentrated enough in a single jurisdiction that Decentralization no longer counts as a standout strength.

key_findings: Monad only partially clears all three of our TradFi baseline checks -- quantum-computer readiness, regulatory footing and security -- but none of those checks is holding the score down. Monad's category-by-category performance already sits below every one of those checks' ceilings. Quantum readiness moved from a fail to a partial pass after Monad published a post-quantum roadmap (September 28, 2026), a draft design for upgradeable account authentication, and research on a quantum-safe consensus design; none of it is live yet. Security stays a partial pass because the major 2026 upgrades (a faster consensus pace in July and a storage redesign in September) have no published independent review; the last published audits date from 2025.

Tokenomics & Supply is Monad's weakest category by a wide margin at 34. Roughly half of the total token supply (about 50.6%) is held by the team, early investors, and the project treasury, all locked behind a single 12-month cliff. When that lock expires on November 24, 2026, roughly 1.4 times the current publicly circulating supply becomes unlockable in a single day -- a major concentration and potential-sell-pressure risk.

Decentralization scores 43. Entry to the validator set is open rather than gated, and about 27 independent entities would need to collude to control a meaningful share of stake -- both real strengths. But validators based in the United States account for about a quarter of the roughly 197 active validators, and that jurisdiction concentration is the binding factor holding the score down. There is still only one client implementation, and in-protocol slashing remains logging-only.

On-Chain Health scores a middling 54. Deposits in Monad applications held at about $817 million in mid-November 2026 after major incentive programs wound down in September, and chain fees roughly doubled since July to about $10,700 a day. But daily active addresses fell from about 18,800 to about 11,000 over the same period, and a large share of the roughly 9 million daily transactions comes from MEV auction bids and trading bots rather than organic use.

TradFi Approved scores 44. Visa added Monad to its stablecoin settlement network on November 10, 2026, so participating card issuers and acquirers can now settle in stablecoins on the chain -- a live link to a major payment network, though no participants or Monad-specific volume have been disclosed. There is still no ETF or exchange-traded product for MON, no regulated MON futures, and no bank or trust charter integration.

Privacy & Confidentiality scores 42, credited mainly to Unlink, a privacy tool that's been live on Monad's mainnet since June 2026. It counts here because it runs as a smart contract directly on Monad rather than as a separate chain with its own security. The score is discounted heavily, though, because it's still young and there's no public data yet on how much it's actually being used.

Monad's TradFi score moved from 49 to 50 in November 2026, on the Visa settlement integration (TradFi Approved 42 to 44) and post-quantum research (Security & Future-Proofing 52 to 55). At a raw score of 49.69 it sits 0.19 points above the line that rounds to 50, and the TradFi Approved move alone is enough to decide that rounding.

Monad earns a full pass on our fast, guaranteed-finality check -- transactions become fully and irreversibly final in about 600 milliseconds following a network upgrade (MIP-12), with new blocks produced roughly every 300 milliseconds. It also runs the same smart-contract environment as Ethereum, so existing agent tooling built for Ethereum generally works here too.

Execution Layer is Monad's strongest category on the AI framework at 86, driven by its fast block times and a built-in feature that streams transaction events in real time -- useful for an agent that needs to react to on-chain activity immediately.
Because Monad's mainnet has been live under a year, it's scored on the actual track record it does have rather than penalized for a longer history it simply hasn't had time to build.

watch_items: On November 24, 2026, the team's tokens begin releasing (about 10.7 billion MON, per the Monad Foundation), and trackers estimate roughly 16.6 billion MON in total including the first investor and treasury tranches -- about 1.4 times the current circulating supply. No lockup extensions were announced. Tokenomics & Supply and On-Chain Health are worth re-assessing once the actual release is visible on-chain.

Major incentive programs on Monad wound down around September 2026, and deposits held at about $817 million rather than falling sharply. Daily active addresses fell by about 40% over the same period; a recovery in organic users would support On-Chain Health, while further declines would weigh on it.

Monad's system for automatically penalizing misbehaving validators currently only logs violations rather than actually enforcing a penalty. This is the single biggest weakness pulling down the Security Posture score on the AI framework, and it's worth checking again at every future review to see if real enforcement has been turned on.

If real usage data for Unlink (Monad's privacy tool) becomes available, it would likely raise the Privacy & Confidentiality score, which is currently held down mainly by the lack of any public evidence of how much it's actually being used.
If validator hosting diversifies away from its current jurisdiction concentration, that would be the clearest path back toward a higher Decentralization score.

Monad's 2026 protocol upgrades (MIP-12 in July and MIP-8 in September) have no published independent security review yet. A published, current audit of these changes would restore full assurance coverage and is the trigger for clearing the remaining gap on the security check.

xStocks announced more than 1,100 tokenized US stocks and ETFs for Monad in October 2026, and Monad's planned Private Settlement feature for institutional payments is expected in the coming months. Neither is credited until live usage can be confirmed; either would be a Real-World Utility or Privacy & Confidentiality re-credit candidate.
